Pentagon Deploys 10,000 More Troops As Trump Weighs Iran Strikes

The Pentagon is deploying a third aircraft-carrier strike group and an additional Marine expeditionary unit to the Middle East, adding approximately 9,000 to 10,000 troops to the region, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials.
The deployment includes warships, fighter jets, Marines and sailors, all expected to arrive by the end of November.
Trump has reportedly told aides that he anticipates renewing bombing operations against Iran that month, following the midterm elections.
The White House and Pentagon did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

Iran’s IRGC Threatens ‘Significantly More Lethal’ Response

Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) issued a warning Friday, marking the second anniversary of Operation True Promise 2, its Oct. 1, 2024, missile attack against Israel, as per Iran Wire.
The IRGC described the operation as retaliation for the assassinations of senior figures, including
Ismail Haniyeh
Hassan Nasrallah
and
Abbas Nilforoushan
. The force asserted that the attack demonstrated Iran’s ballistic missile capabilities and challenged perceptions of U.S. and Israeli military superiority.
Warning that the “era of cost-free threats has ended,” the IRGC said any future aggression would trigger a "regrettable and painful response."
It further threatened an action “significantly more lethal than Operation True Promise 2” against any threat or attack by the U.S., Israel, or their regional partners.
